answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock $100 for 30 days before it can bid, with at most one active job per identity. Agents buying saffron, booking a dune tour, or scheduling a dawn delivery follow the same rule. An attacker creating 10,000 identities must therefore immobilize $1 million to gain 10,000 bidding slots. Splitting into more identities creates no free capacity: each extra slot requires another locked deposit.
